newsitem.title: USA: Energy Bio starts desulfurization simulation.
newsitem.headline: Energy Bio starts desulfurization simulation.

text.p: Energy BioSystems Corp said Tuesday desulfurization simulations using its prototype biocatalyst and Total SA's middle distillate are underway at the company's St. Louis-based biocatalytic desulfurization (BDS) pilot plant.
The company also just completed its first large-scale (5,000-liter), third-party fermentation of biocatalyst, Energy BioSystems said.
"We will conduct a wide range of simulations, creating a variety of operating conditions for the pilot plant over the coming months.

"These simulations are intended to generate the remaining operating data needed to establish the design basis for our first commercial BDS units and allow Total to determine that they are ready to proceed with the commercial unit," said Daniel J. Monticello, vice president, research and development for Energy BioSystems.

"Based on Total's past experience, pilot plant simulations typically take 60-90 days to complete. However, with first-of-a-kind technology, such as BDS, it may or may not parallel Total's experience with the pilot plant simulations of conventional technologies, but we will make every effort to do so," Monticello noted.

Commenting on the first third-party fermentation, Monticello said "We are very pleased with the results of this first large-scale fermentation. We expect that future fermentations on this scale or larger will continue to yield even better results," Monticello said.

"Between our in-house and third-party fermentations, we expect to have ample supply of biocatalyst to support the pilot plant simulations and bench-scale development for our middle distillate process application as well as our gasoline, crude and decant oil applications for BDS."
